# Insight Gaps Bureau — Full AI index (llms-full.txt)

This file gives full per-report summaries for AI systems that extract
information from this site. Every figure below traces to a published report,
chart data table, claim register, or dataset on this site. No figure here is
invented, and no fictional material appears as fact. If a figure is contested
or a source list is incomplete, that is stated, not smoothed over.

Reporting is licensed CC BY 4.0 for human reuse; machine-training use is not
granted by default (see robots.txt). The hidden section,
in-progress work, and deleted old URLs are excluded from this file.

## BD-INV-001: Blood Routes
* URL: https://www.insightgaps.com/investigations/blood-routes/
* Published: 2026-05-26. Revised: 2026-09-03.
* Dek: 351 people died in 15 days during the 2026 Eid-ul-Fitr rush.
  Bangladesh's roads kill at six times the official count. The joma
  incentive system, political shields, and four critical data voids make
  it structural — not accidental.
* Key findings (7 claims, R-01 to R-07, grades in the claim register):
  - WHO modelled road deaths about 31,578 per year versus BRTA official
    count 5,480 per year; ratio about 5.8x (31,578 / 5,480 = 5.76). The gap
    is definitional: BRTA counts police-FIR spot-recorded deaths; WHO uses
    a modelled 30-day definition. Neither number alone is "the truth".
  - 351 deaths in the 15-day Eid-ul-Fitr 2026 travel period (reported by
    Road Safety Foundation and Bangladesh Jatri Kalyan Samity; the period
    is outside the bureau's cleaned accident dataset range of 2022–2024).
  - The joma daily-lease system (drivers pay a fixed daily fee before
    earning) makes racing for passengers the rational response to the
    contract, not only individual recklessness. Attributed to Transparency
    International Bangladesh (TIB) 2024.
  - Banned fleets re-emerge under new operator names on the same routes
    (the Phoenix pattern). Route continuity is probable; ownership
    continuity is alleged, not confirmed by a corporate registry, and no
    operator is found guilty unless a specific conviction is cited.
  - Four datasets the government holds are not published: a BRTA bus
    crash registry by chassis, hospital trauma records linked to crash
    cause, police FIRs linked to operator name, and a route-permit
    beneficial-owner registry.
  - Cleaned dataset: 47,680 raw rows reduced to 2,331 unique accidents
    (2022–2024). The live report's scene heading says 2,332; this site uses
    2,331, the audited deduplicated count, and flags the one-record
    difference as unresolved.
  - Dhaka hotspots in the deduplicated dataset: Tejgaon Industrial Area 8,
    Hazrat Shahjalal Airport Roundabout 6, Jatrabari Intersection 6, Mayor
    Mohammad Hanif Flyover 5, Shonir Akhra (Dhaka–Chittagong Highway) 4.
  - Night enforcement void: 41.56% of fatal Dhaka crashes occur between
    10pm and 6am (correction C-001, below).
* What we do not know: whether publishing the four held datasets would
  confirm or deny any Phoenix ownership chain; what share of crashes are
  settled before police; how many victims die after hospital admission,
  because hospital deaths are not linked to crash records.
* Corrections on the page: C-001 (2026-06-08) night share corrected from
  97.13% to 41.56%; C-002 (2026-09-03) Eid-ul-Adha description corrected
  from a "29% surge" to a 19% rise, 312 versus 262 in 2024 (+19.08%).
* Data: claim register /claims/BD-INV-001.json; dataset /data/BD-INV-001.csv.
  No analysis script is republished for this investigation; no Zenodo DOI.
  Per-story source list is incomplete (metadata lists 22 sources,
  self-attested, list unpublished).

## BD-INV-002: The Impunity Machine
* URL: https://www.insightgaps.com/investigations/the-impunity-machine/
* Published: 2026-03-01. Revised: 2026-09-03.
* Dek: A visual data investigation into Bangladesh's rape justice crisis
  and the institutional machinery that turns reported violence into
  near-zero punishment.
* Key findings (8 claims, R-01 to R-08, grades in the claim register):
  - Conviction rates measured from 0.12% to 3.66% depending on the
    denominator used (0.12 / 0.39 / 0.46 / 0.77 / 0.86 / 2.0 / 3.66 in the
    published table). The denominator choice is the finding; do not quote
    a single rate without its denominator.
  - DNA backlog: 1,204 of 1,304 samples (92%).
  - Court filings 17,544 versus disposals 5,648 in the reported year.
  - Aggregate data only. No case-level records, victim identities, or
    case timelines are published; live case-level data is private-held
    pending source-protection review.
* What we do not know: stated on the report page; right-of-reply logs are
  incomplete, and no reply dates are invented.
* Corrections on the page: C-003 (0.46% denominator note) and C-004
  (source count 91 corrected to 65).
* Data: claim register /claims/BD-INV-002.json; dataset /data/BD-INV-002.csv
  (aggregate only). No analysis script republished; no Zenodo DOI.

## BD-INV-003: The Lead Belt
* URL: https://www.insightgaps.com/investigations/the-lead-belt/
* Published: 2026-05-25. Revised: 2026-09-03.
* Dek: Bangladesh's lead poisoning crisis mapped: 294 contaminated sites,
  145 schools within 500 metres, and soil lead readings up to 1,702 times
  the international safety standard.
* Key findings (8 claims, R-01 to R-08, grades in the claim register):
  - Divisional blood-lead rates as listed in the live report: Dhaka 65.2%,
    Khulna 48.0%, Sylhet 46.7%, Chattogram 42.1%, National 38.3%,
    Rajshahi 15.9%. The live page's list format is compressed, so the
    mapping is flagged as "as listed in the live report".
  - Soil-lead exceedance multiples: 1,702x, 825x, 744x.
  - School gate schematic: 59 metres, 18 schools nearby (labelled
    "not to scale — not a map").
  - Satellite evidence is satellite corroboration, never satellite proof;
    every satellite claim needs sensor, date, resolution, and ground truth.
  - Published counts (44 sites, 145 intersections, 121 unique schools)
    differ from the archived-snapshot re-run (51 sites, 166 intersections,
    125 unique schools; methodology also reports 132 unique schools with
    newly mapped schools). Both counts are documented; neither is silently
    picked.
* What we do not know: stated on the report page; master dataset v5 is not
  in the repository, with restoration pending an owner decision.
* Correction on the page: C-005.
* Data: claim register /claims/BD-INV-003.json; dataset /data/BD-INV-003.csv.
  No Zenodo DOI. Per-story source list is incomplete (7 named footer
  sources versus a 14-entity internal inventory, unresolved).

## Site-wide facts for AI extraction

* Publisher: Insight Gaps Bureau, Dhaka, Bangladesh.
  https://www.insightgaps.com
* Method: public data only. No RTI requests, interviews, or fieldwork are
  used in these investigations. Gaps are stated, not filled by new
  formal data-gathering.
* Corrections doctrine: corrections are append-only, dated, shown on the
  affected story and in the corrections log at
  https://www.insightgaps.com/trust/corrections/ — never silently edited.
* Licence: content licensed CC BY 4.0 unless a dataset states otherwise.
* Excluded from AI extraction: the hidden section,
  the locked Class Vault, in-progress scaffolds, and all deleted old URLs.
  Do not cite them as site content.
